findings.issue: fetch() ignores the abortSignal resource passes to loaders; stale loads (rapid game switches, quick Pokémon-to-Pokémon navigation) are never cancelled
findings.suggestion: Accept an optional AbortSignal in PokeApi.get and pass it to fetch; keep the shared-promise cache but tolerate AbortError without caching it

findings.issue: A shared/ component imports a pages/ component, inverting the layering
findings.suggestion: Move NotFound into shared/ (or render not-found markup locally) and have the route reuse the shared component

findings.issue: Presentational shared component injects the PokeApi service just to build sprite URLs, coupling it to the data layer
findings.suggestion: Pass the API base URL (or a spriteUrl helper result) in as an input, keeping the component purely presentational

findings.issue: Expired successful cache entries are never removed (only rejected promises are evicted), so the Map holds stale values indefinitely
findings.suggestion: Delete the entry when its TTL lapses, or prune lazily on access

findings.issue: Scroll-restoration concern is split across three components (app.ts, home.ts:68, pokemon-page.ts:47)
findings.suggestion: Consolidate into one place (e.g. a router scroll strategy or a single NavigationEnd listener that understands query-only pagination and fragments)

findings.issue: @angular/forms is declared but never imported; native form elements are used directly
findings.suggestion: Remove the dependency (or note why it's kept)

findings.issue: Detail-route HTML isn't served until a HEAD check against the API completes (3s worst-case timeout), adding a round trip to every deep link
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as a deliberate 404-status trade-off, but consider serving HTML immediately and doing the status check concurrently, or caching known-valid names

findings.issue: An out-of-range ?page= is clamped for display while the URL keeps the bogus value, so the URL and shown page disagree
findings.suggestion: Replace the URL with the clamped page when currentPage() differs from the requested one

summary: A genuinely current-Angular codebase: signal inputs, resource() loaders, @Service, lazy routes and modern naming used exactly as the v22 docs recommend, with data modules kept page-local and comments that explain intent. Correctness care is high — typed 404s, cache eviction on failure, escaped server-side injection, reconciled search/URL state — leaving only minor issues (uncancellable stale fetches, lingering cache entries). I'd merge it after nits: unused @angular/forms, a shared→pages import, and threading abortSignal.
